xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2066: OKF v2 — knowledge viewer: inkeep open-knowledge coinstall (progressive), /okf open, dashboard Knowledge page

plan.title: OKF v2 — knowledge viewer: inkeep open-knowledge coinstall (progressive), /okf open, dashboard Knowledge page
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: OKF v1 (#2468) shipped the /okf skill and a PR-gated knowledge bundle, but there is no GUI: no graph wiki-link viewer, no WYSIWYG browsing, and the old 'MCP read server' deferred item is unaddressed. inkeep/open-knowledge is exactly the right shape (editor + graph viewer + MCP over markdown-with-frontmatter folders) but is GPL-3.0 and must stay at arm's length from MIT @overdeck/*.
narratives.Proposal: Adopt @inkeep/open-knowledge as a separately-installed global binary (`ok`), never imported. Progressive install via ensureOpenKnowledge() in src/lib/installers/open-knowledge.ts (ensureOllama/ensureMnemos pattern, injectable seams, Node-24 diagnosis). New `pan knowledge open` + `/okf open` resolve the bundle via the canonical resolveKnowledgeBundleRoot() read door, ensure the binary, and start/reuse a local `ok start` server. The dashboard gains a Knowledge tab whose server owns the ok subprocess lifecycle (lazy spawn, health, reuse, shutdown kill) and reverse-proxies it (HTTP+WS) under /knowledge-viewer/* for same-origin embedding at https://overdeck.localhost, with graceful states for no-bundle / not-installed / starting / embedded / embed-blocked. A round-trip spike gates only the edit-in-viewer posture: if frontmatter round-trips lossily, the page ships read-only. MCP wiring via `ok init` is documented, opt-in, never automated.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No eager install: pan install only mentions the viewer, never installs @inkeep/open-knowledge
- No import/require/bundling of @inkeep/open-knowledge anywhere in @overdeck/* (GPL isolation; subprocess + HTTP only)
- No Node upgrade automation: Node 24 is ok's requirement; detect and report only, dashboard stays Node 22
- No lease-based concurrent write mode (deferred item #3 — successor issue)
- No LLM semantic auditor in the merge gate (deferred item #5 — successor issue; the conformance gate stays deterministic Python)
- No bespoke viz.html graph visualizer (retired in favor of open-knowledge's viewer)
- No automatic MCP registration by Overdeck (documented opt-in via ok init only)
- No second bundle resolver: all resolution goes through resolveKnowledgeBundleRoot()
- No degradation of any existing dashboard surface when the binary/bundle is absent or the user opts out
- No auto-discovery via projects.yaml, post-merge auto-sync, knowledge-health surface, or pan sync distribution (tracked separately once this lands)

autoDecisions.summary: Reused the canonical PRD on overdeck-state instead of authoring a new one.
autoDecisions.rationale: It is 2 days old, written as an executable implementation brief, and every file reference re-verified clean against HEAD 9e8c19eddc.

autoDecisions.summary: Placed ensureOpenKnowledge() in src/lib/installers/open-knowledge.ts instead of the PRD's src/lib/open-knowledge.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: The src/lib/installers/ convention (ensureMnemos) postdates the PRD and src/cli/commands/knowledge.ts already imports from it; contract and tests from WI-2 are unchanged.

autoDecisions.summary: The installer module also exports the shared `ok start` launcher used by both the CLI verb and the dashboard viewer service.
autoDecisions.rationale: One launch path avoids duplicate spawn/health logic and keeps flag-spelling fixes (hazard H2) in one place.

autoDecisions.summary: The pan knowledge open CLI change updates sync-sources/skills/pan-knowledge/SKILL.md in the same commit.
autoDecisions.rationale: The wrapper skill exists (PRD predates it) and scripts/lint-skills.sh fails CI on drift; the skills convention requires same-commit updates.

autoDecisions.summary: Auto-install defaults ON for explicit user gestures (/okf open, pan knowledge open, dashboard Install button) and OFF unattended.
autoDecisions.rationale: PRD Decision 3 states exactly this; both surfaces are explicit gestures, and unattended flows must never trigger a global npm install.

autoDecisions.summary: The round-trip spike runs first as a work item with its verdict posted to PAN-2066 and recorded in continue.json, gating only page copy.
autoDecisions.rationale: PRD WI-1/FR-6 define the fallback (read-only posture) so lossiness never blocks the integration; no code diff exists to inspect, so no inspection gate.

autoDecisions.summary: The docs item creates docs/ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS.md for the open-knowledge credit.
autoDecisions.rationale: No acknowledgements doc exists yet (PAN-1474 unshipped); creating it is the smallest change that satisfies the PRD's credit requirement.

items.title: Round-trip verification spike: does open-knowledge preserve frontmatter losslessly?

expected_outputs: PAN-2066 carries a comment stating the lossless/lossy verdict with git diff evidence
metadata.acJustification: Manual spike whose only outputs are the issue comment and the recorded posture decision; two ACs cover both.

narrative.Action: Install @inkeep/open-knowledge manually (npm install -g), open a scratch git copy of ../overdeck-knowledge with `ok start`, edit one concept file in the UI, save, and inspect `git diff`. Check: YAML frontmatter key order and unknown keys preserved; index.md and log.md untouched; no trailing-whitespace/EOL churn. Also capture `ok --help` output for the launcher flags (hazard H2). Post the verdict with diff evidence as a comment on PAN-2066. Record the resulting Knowledge-page posture (editable vs read-only) as a decision in .overdeck/continue.json. Fallback per FR-6: lossy ⇒ the Knowledge page ships read-only ('view and search; edit via /okf author'); the integration proceeds either way.

items.title: Given a scratch copy of the knowledge bundle, when one concept is edited and saved in the open-knowledge UI, the agent posts a PAN-2066 comment that states the lossless/lossy verdict and includes the git diff evidence

ensureOpenKnowledge() progressive installer with Node-24 diagnosis

expected_outputs: open-knowledge installer tests pass with zero real-timer waits (fake timers only)

narrative.Action: New file src/lib/installers/open-knowledge.ts modeled on src/lib/ollama.ts and src/lib/installers/mnemos.ts: EnsureOpenKnowledgeOptions with injectable runCommand, installOpenKnowledge (default: `npm install -g @inkeep/open-knowledge`), maxHealthAttempts, retryDelayMs, sleep. Health = `ok --version` exits 0. On install/launch failure run `node --version`; if major < 24 the error message must read: `open-knowledge requires Node 24+; found <v>. Install Node 24+ or run '/okf open --no-install' after installing manually.` Never a silent fallback. Also export a startOpenKnowledgeServer(bundlePath, opts) launcher helper (async spawn, injectable, port probing per PRD Decision 2 — verify actual `ok start` flags from the spike's `ok --help` capture) for reuse by the CLI verb and the dashboard service. Tests mirror src/lib/__tests__/ollama.test.ts with vi.useFakeTimers().

Dashboard viewer lifecycle service (spawn / health / reuse / shutdown kill)

expected_outputs: knowledge-viewer service tests pass with fake timers for all health-poll delays
metadata.parallelSafeReason: New isolated service file plus its own new test file; no file overlaps with any sibling wave item.

narrative.Action: New src/dashboard/server/services/knowledge-viewer.ts: getOrStartViewer(projectKey) → { port, url }. Resolves the bundle via the canonical resolver, spawns `ok start` through the shared launcher from src/lib/installers/open-knowledge.ts (async spawn only — no execSync), health-polls the port with awaited setTimeout sleeps, tracks one process per project in a module map, reuses a healthy process on subsequent calls, and registers cleanup on the server shutdown path (the handleShutdownSignal flow in src/dashboard/server/ws-terminal.ts / server.ts) so dashboard exit kills the subprocess. Absent binary or absent bundle returns a typed status instead of throwing (NFR-4). Unit tests inject spawn/health/sleep; vi.useFakeTimers() for every delay.

items.title: getOrStartViewer spawns ok start for the resolved bundle via async spawn and returns port and url once the health check passes
Given a healthy running viewer, a second getOrStartViewer call returns the same port without spawning a second process — exactly one ok process per project
The registered shutdown cleanup kills the ok subprocess, leaving no orphan process after the dashboard exits
Spawn failure or health-poll timeout rejects with an actionable error instead of hanging; absent binary or bundle returns a typed not-available status
Knowledge-viewer API routes + same-origin reverse proxy (HTTP + WS)

expected_outputs: route tests pass for status/install/start endpoints
server build succeeds (boot-path change must be runtime-boot-tested before live restart)
metadata.parallelSafeReason: New route module and new test file; the only shared file (server.ts route composition) is touched by no other item in the plan.

narrative.Action: New route module src/dashboard/server/routes/knowledge-viewer.ts composed in server.ts: GET /api/knowledge-viewer/status (reports installed / bundle-configured / running truthfully for every combination, never throws for absent pieces), POST /api/knowledge-viewer/install (invokes ensureOpenKnowledge with autoInstall: true — explicit user gesture), POST /api/knowledge-viewer/start (delegates to viewer-service, returns the proxied URL). Reverse proxy for /knowledge-viewer/* → the ok server: HTTP via async request piping, WebSocket via the upgrade-event pattern of ws-terminal.ts (monkey-patched upgrade listener that passes non-matching paths through). No execSync. This touches the server boot path — per repo rule, boot-test the built dist in a throwaway instance before any live restart; never hot-patch.

items.title: GET /api/knowledge-viewer/status returns truthful installed/bundle/running state for each combination (no bundle, not installed, installed idle, running) without throwing

POST /api/knowledge-viewer/start starts or reuses the viewer and returns its /knowledge-viewer/ proxied URL
The server routes /knowledge-viewer/* requests (HTTP and WebSocket upgrades) to the ok server so the viewer UI renders same-origin at the dashboard URL
